116

121	      `toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on owner`

201	      <evidence>", Blockers "None.".
202	- [ ] Leftover worktrees and branches for the item are listed and offered for
203	      removal.

206	
207	```text
208	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>'
209	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --quote '<his exact words>'
210	toolkit work finish <id> --by <owner> --evidence '<what shows it works>' --allow-open-sub-items
211	```
212	
213	The second is only for a result approval not yet recorded. The third is only
214	for a parent the owner said is done while sub-items are still open; quote his
215	words in a history note. The command sets Next action and Resume here, and
216	prints what still needs a note.
217	
218	The finish command also backs up `.work-items/` and `.memory/` (and Hindsight
219	memory) to the owner's backup folder and prints one line about it. Read that
220	line:

225	  `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or `none` when he wants no backup).
226	- A line with "failed" or "Tell the owner": tell him that line as it is. The
227	  item is still Done; only the backup is missing.
228

230	
231	Asked by `work-finish`. Only `toolkit work cancel` sets Cancelled.
232

234	- [ ] Each open sub-item: ask whether to cancel it, move it to the top level,
235	      or move it under another item. Never cancel them without asking.
236	- [ ] `toolkit work cancel <id> --reason '<his words>'`
237	
238	Cancelling keeps the record. Nothing is deleted.
239	
240	## 7. Delivery offer
241	
242	Only `work-delegate` makes the offer and records the answer. Every other skill
243	opens `work-delegate` for it. The recorded value:
244	
245	```text
246	toolkit work set <id> --delivery agent-led
247	toolkit work set <id> --delivery owner-led
248	```
249	
250	A delivery answer never approves requirements, a design, or a result, and
251	never widens merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.
252	
253	## 8. Project-wide decision
254	
255	Recorded by `work-decide` as a row in `DECISIONS.md` at the project root,
256	then committed through `publish-docs`.
257	
258	```text
259	toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner>
260	toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner> --replaces D-<n>
261	```
262	
263	`DECISIONS.md` is append-only. A changed decision is a new row that names the
264	one it replaces. Any skill that meets a project-wide decision opens
265	`work-decide`, which runs the full order of work with `publish-docs`.
266	
267	## 9. Memory proposal
268	
269	A memory the owner did not answer ("Save to memory?") is saved as a proposal:
270	status `needs-review`. The agent does not rely on it until he approves it.
271	
272	```text
273	toolkit memory approve <key> --by <owner>
274	toolkit memory reject <key>
275	```
276	
277	A rejection deletes the proposal. Never propose the same fact again in other
278	words.
279	
280	## 10. Sub-items and approvals
281	
282	- A child made with `--covers R-02,R-03` links those parent requirements and
283	  inherits the parent's requirements approval. The owner is never asked to
284	  approve the same requirement twice.
285	- A parent design the owner approved covers its `--covers` children: they
286	  start at planning (stage 06) with no design of their own.
287	- A child that needs new behavior gets its own `R-xx` and its own approval.
288	- Each sub-item needs its own result approval. The owner's approval of the
289	  parent does not cover it.
290	- Finishing a sub-item never finishes or approves its parent.
291	
292	## 11. Standing merge instruction
293	
294	A merge normally needs the owner's yes to that merge. A standing merge
295	instruction replaces that yes only when all of these hold:
296	
297	- [ ] `DECISIONS.md` records it as the owner's decision (the project's
298	      `AGENTS.md` may point at it);
299	- [ ] an `acceptance-checker` that did not build the change reported no
300	      blocking issue on that exact head commit;
301	- [ ] every check passes on that head;
302	- [ ] the work item does not say its merge needs the owner's approval (an
303	      item that says so overrides the instruction).
304	
305	Without an independent check the instruction does not apply: ask the owner.
306	A new commit after the check means a new check on the new head.
307	
308	## 12. When an approve command refuses
309	
310	- Show the owner the command's error in plain words. Never work around it by
311	  editing the record, the design text, or a header field.
312	- The error names what is missing (for example the Agreed goal still holds
313	  the template text). Fix that, then run the same command again.
314	- Exit code 2 means a refused gate: the record is unchanged.

prints what still needs a note.

line:

- "Backed up ... to <folder>": done. Say it in one line in the reply.
- "No backup folder is set ...": ask the owner for a folder outside the

  `toolkit config set backup.dir <folder>` (or `none` when he wants no backup).

  item is still Done; only the backup is missing.

opens `work-delegate` for it. The recorded value:

```text

toolkit work set <id> --delivery owner-led
```

A delivery answer never approves requirements, a design, or a result, and
never widens merge, deployment, spending, or publishing.

Recorded by `work-decide` as a row in `DECISIONS.md` at the project root,
then committed through `publish-docs`.

```text
toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner>
toolkit decision add --decision '<decision>' --why '<why>' --by <owner> --replaces D-<n>
```

`DECISIONS.md` is append-only. A changed decision is a new row that names the
one it replaces. Any skill that meets a project-wide decision opens
`work-decide`, which runs the full order of work with `publish-docs`.

## 9. Memory proposal

A memory the owner did not answer ("Save to memory?") is saved as a proposal:
status `needs-review`. The agent does not rely on it until he approves it.


words.

  inherits the parent's requirements approval. The owner is never asked to
  approve the same requirement twice.

  start at planning (stage 06) with no design of their own.
- A child that needs new behavior gets its own `R-xx` and its own approval.
- Each sub-item needs its own result approval. The owner's approval of the
  parent does not cover it.
- Finishing a sub-item never finishes or approves its parent.

A merge normally needs the owner's yes to that merge. A standing merge
instruction replaces that yes only when all of these hold:

- [ ] `DECISIONS.md` records it as the owner's decision (the project's
      `AGENTS.md` may point at it);
- [ ] an `acceptance-checker` that did not build the change reported no
      blocking issue on that exact head commit;
- [ ] every check passes on that head;
- [ ] the work item does not say its merge needs the owner's approval (an

- The error names what is missing (for example the Agreed goal still holds

# The spec check

How to run the `requirements-analyst` check on an item's requirements and
turn its findings into fixes or questions for the owner.

## When it runs

- Before asking for the requirements approval.
- Whenever the owner says "check the spec".
- Again after a change to an approved requirement.

## The brief

Give the `requirements-analyst` agent (Claude Code: `work:requirements-analyst`;
Codex: the text of `references/agent-requirements-analyst.md`) this, pasted
in, because it has no tracker access:

1. The item id.
2. The Starting request, the Agreed goal, every `R-xx` block, the Acceptance
   list, and the open questions.
3. The area's file in `requirements/` when one exists, so it can spot a
   conflict.
4. The job: "Check these requirements before design. Return ready or not
   ready, then each finding with a fix."
5. Files it may write: nothing.

## What it returns

Ready or not ready, then findings of these kinds, each with a fix:

- missing pieces (a step, a person, an error case, a state, a boundary with
  another system, a way to tell it worked);
- places not explicit end to end;
- wording a builder could misread;
- build details inside requirements;
- drift from the Agreed goal;
- research or history in the wrong place.

## Handling the findings

- For each finding, propose a fix in plain words: what to change, where, and
  what the line would say instead.
- Change nothing without the owner's yes. Three findings or fewer: one
  decision per message, in order. More than three: one numbered list he can
  answer in one message. That list is the only exception to one question per
  message.
- A dismissed finding stays dismissed for this item in this session.
- Two sources that disagree (the item and the area file in `requirements/`,
  for example): name both, quote the disagreement, and let the owner pick.
  Never silently prefer the newer or longer one.
- Do not turn the check into a rewrite. Personal wording taste is not a
  finding.
- A clean spec: say so in one line and move on to the approval question.

## Example findings for the owner

Two findings: the first message asks about the first one only.

```markdown
The spec check found 2 things. The first:

R-02 says "large exports finish quickly". A builder cannot test "quickly".
I recommend: "An export of 50,000 rows finishes in under one minute."
Use this wording?
```

Four findings: one numbered list.

```markdown
The spec check found 4 things. Answer each by number, for example "1 yes, 2 no".

1. R-02 says "large exports finish quickly". A builder cannot test "quickly".
   Fix: "An export of 50,000 rows finishes in under one minute." Use this?
2. Nothing says what a person without manager access sees. Fix: add R-03,
   "People who are not managers do not see the Export button." Add it?
3. R-01 and the Acceptance list name different file types (CSV and Excel).
   Fix: CSV in both. Use CSV?
4. Nothing says what happens when the report has no rows. Fix: add R-04,
   "An empty report exports a file with only the column names." Add it?
```

## Findings

### Misreading risks

1. **R-02 rule 4 does not cover every accented letter.**
   - Wording: "Accented letters become their plain letter ("Café" → `cafe`)."
   - Wrong reading: remove only accent marks that can be split off a letter. Then "ß", "ø", "æ", "ł" and "đ" become punctuation under R-05, so "Straße" prints `stra-e` and "Søren" prints `s-ren`.
   - Intended reading: probably that every Latin letter with an accent or stroke ends up as plain letters.
   - Consequence: the builder and the tester can each pick a different reading and both believe they are correct.
   - Fix: "Latin letters with accents or strokes become plain letters: é→e, ø→o, ł→l, đ→d, ß→ss, æ→ae, œ→oe. Letters from other alphabets follow R-05." Add the acceptance check `node slug.js "Straße Søren"` → `strasse-soren`.

2. **R-03 does not say where the usage message goes.**
   - Wording: "prints `Usage: node slug.js "<title>"` as an error message."
   - Risk: "as an error message" could mean the text itself or the output channel. The acceptance check "nothing on normal output" only holds if the message goes to the error output.
   - Fix: "prints `Usage: node slug.js "<title>"` on standard error (the error output), prints nothing on standard output, and exits with code 1."

### Missing

3. **No rule for a title that starts with a dash.**
   - Example: under R-04, `node slug.js --help` or `node slug.js -x` counts as a title and prints `help` or `x`.

   - Fix: add one line to R-04, either "Arguments that start with `-` are title text like any other" or "`--help` and `-h` print the usage message on standard output and exit with code 0." Pick one.

R-01, R-03's trigger cases, R-04's joining rule, R-05's list of allowed characters, and the Acceptance list agree with each other and with the Agreed goal. There are no build details, research notes, or drift inside the `R-xx` blocks.
